rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Shuʿayb’s people suffer the same fate as Lot’s nearby people, linking this account to the earlier Lot narrative.
rows.anchor: It is evident from the last verse that Shu‘ayb’s nation too met the same fate

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The disbelievers’ erasure from their settlement reverses their threat to expel Shuʿayb and his followers.
rows.anchor: While referring to this threat, it is said that they themselves were wiped out from their settlement as if they never existed.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The second sentence reverses the disbelievers’ warning that Shuʿayb’s followers would incur a great loss: the rejectors themselves lost.
rows.anchor: those who rejected Shu‘ayb (sws) were the ones who had incurred a loss.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Parallel wording is omitted, a common Qur’anic feature; the understood structure supplies the glorifying verb for the angels as well as the thunder.
rows.anchor: parallel words have been suppressed which is a common feature of Qur’ ānic Arabic. Thus the actual structure is like this

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Tasbih absolves God of negative attributes, while hamd acknowledges His noble attributes.
rows.anchor: God is absolved of negative attributes

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The angels continually glorify and praise God out of fear that He may command them at any time, unlike the disbelievers demanding punishment.
rows.anchor: while the disbelievers have the audacity to demand divine punishment, the angels are continuously glorifying and praising God fearing they could be given any directive

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God may send punishment on whomever He wills while people continue disputing about Him.
rows.anchor: God will His lash of punishment to whomsoever He wants while people are still disputing about Him.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The section frames those who demand punishment while relying on self-proclaimed deities as calling for their own doom.
rows.anchor: those who are demanding God’s punishment while relying on their self-proclaimed deities are only calling for their own doom

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: There are no divine associates; God alone is one.
rows.anchor: There are no associates of God. He is the one and only.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Calling any supposed deity is ultimately calling God.
rows.anchor: So whenever a person calls on some deity He is actually calling on God.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Calling God alone is beneficial and blessed because all authority and control belong to Him.
rows.anchor: What is implied is that only calling God is beneficial, consequential and blessed. This is because all authority and control are with Him.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Those who call on others receive no answer; these supposed deities hear nothing because they do not exist.
rows.anchor: All those who call others will never be answered by them. These deities or partners of God hear nothing because they do not even exist.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The verse uses the mirage image to portray the futility of calling other deities.
rows.anchor: The verse then cites the example of a mirage to portray this situation.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Everything obeys God by its existence; people who misuse their choice still live within His law, and arrogance rebels against their own nature.
rows.anchor: everything by its actual existence obeys God. If they who have been given some freedom of choice misuse this freedom

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Shadows illustrate subjection to God’s law: they prostrate at night, rise slowly at dawn, then prostrate again as the sun descends at midday.
rows.anchor: even the shadows of things prostrate at night and slowly lift their heads at dawn

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The shadow image is insinuative reasoning: it directs the mind to a symbol’s reality through human nature rather than formal logic.
rows.anchor: This is a special form of reasoning called insinuation. In it, attention of the mind is directed to the reality of a symbol.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Qul can mean to ask or raise a question, with context deciding its use.
rows.anchor: also implies “to ask and to raise a question.” Context decides its usage.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: If people acknowledge God as master of the heavens and earth, they must explain why they set up other guardians and deities.
rows.anchor: when they acknowledge that God is the master of the heavens and the earth, then on what logic have they set up other guardians and deities?

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Sight and blindness refer to intellectual and moral insight or its absence; darkness is moral darkness and light is the radiance of intellect and faith.
rows.anchor: Vision and blindness referred to in the verse relates to intellectual and moral vision and blindness.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The plural for darkness and singular for light signify many forms of moral and intellectual disorder but one path to moral and intellectual radiance.
rows.anchor: the door to intellectual and moral radiance is just one.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Polytheism assumes God treats darkness and light, or the blind and sighted, as equal, contradicting truth and justice.
rows.anchor: in the sight of God, darkness and light, the blind and those with eyesight are equal.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: If truth and justice are uprooted, the world becomes purposeless, useful only for entertainment.
rows.anchor: they have actually razed down the foundations of truth and justice on which the heavens and the earth stand.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The verse challenges polytheists to show whether their partners created anything like God, making the identity of creation ambiguous.
rows.anchor: have they too created anything like God creates so that the matter has become ambiguous to them

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Al-Qahhar means the one who controls and has authority over everyone.
rows.anchor: means someone who has control and authority over everyone.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Since God alone creates everything and rules over all, there is no need to set up partners.
rows.anchor: when He is also the creator and has authority over all, then what is the need in the first place to set up these partners?

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Section III presents polytheism as uprooting the truth and justice on which the world rests, in conflict with the testimony of the universe’s laws.
rows.anchor: polytheism uproots the whole system of truth and justice on which this world stands

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The section alludes to truth’s victory over the evil opposed to it by the Qur’an’s revelation, with evil blown away like froth.
rows.anchor: a very subtle allusion is given to the victory of the truth over evil in this conflict created between them due to the Qur’ ān’s revelation.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Verse 17 advances the preceding argument in 13:16: polytheistic equivalence conflicts with the universe’s nature and God’s established practice.
rows.anchor: Here, in this verse, one step ahead is taken and it is stated that these things are against the nature of this universe as well

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The water parable shows froth dissipating while useful water remains in the earth for its inhabitants.
rows.anchor: froth is dissipated and water which is beneficial for the earth and its inhabitants remains in the earth.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: In the metal parable, impurities rise and evaporate when silver or another metal is melted, leaving the silver.
rows.anchor: after melting silver or any other metal in a pot, the filth comes to the surface and evaporates and the silver remains.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Together the parables show that the universe preserves what is beneficial and destroys what is not.
rows.anchor: It wants to keep intact what is beneficial and destroy what is not.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God’s established practice pits truth against falsehood: falsehood’s froth evaporates while what benefits people remains.
rows.anchor: He makes truth and falsehood strike one another. As a result of this collision, the froth of falsehood that appears is made to evaporate

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The rain in the parable represents the divine revelation now coming down.
rows.anchor: the rain which is pouring down now in the form of divine revelation
